subject: Provisioning scenarios & activation schedule — OrionBio dedicated capacity

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-14T09:02:00-08:00
Subject: Provisioning scenarios & activation schedule — OrionBio dedicated capacity

Hi Morgan —

Thanks for the time earlier. Attached is a short proposal with three provisioning scenarios we discussed and an activation cadence that maps to your expected Q1 throughput growth. High level:

- Option A — Sprint (short runway): 16-GPU headstart (1 x 8-GPU + 1 x 8-GPU), burst path to 48 GPUs by week 6. Low commitment, higher per-token unit.
- Option B — Maintain (balanced): 64 GPUs baseline (8 x 8-GPU nodes), minimum-guarantee 32 GPUs with reserved lanes for peak. Ramp to 96 GPUs over 10 weeks. Best mix of cost predictability and latency SLO.
- Option C — Scale (95th percentile throughput): 128 GPUs committed, 8-week phased activation (16 -> 48 -> 96 -> 128), includes auto-burst buffer and a lower unit price.

Key notes in the attached: minimum guaranteed GPU terms, activation windows, pause/resume flexibility, and proposed SLA exceptions for model warm-start on your initial heavy inference windows.

Action items I recommend: please confirm the quadrant (A/B/C) that aligns with internal finance appetite; if you want a custom hybrid (e.g., 48 baseline + burst to 80) we can sketch that quickly.

Attachments: orion_proposal_v2.pdf, activation_timeline.xlsx

Rafael
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0187

Redwood Inference — Production-first inference.
From: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@orionbio.ai>

Cc: procurement@orionbio.ai
Date: 2026-12-14T11:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Provisioning scenarios & activation schedule — OrionBio dedicated capacity

Rafael —

Thanks for the options and the clear breakdown. A few quick clarifications from our side before we loop in finance:

1) Minimum guarantee: our CFO is uncomfortable with anything above a 32-GPU minimum for the annual commitment. Is there room to structure Option B with a 32-GPU floor but keep a pricing step-down if we hit utilization thresholds?
2) Ramp timing: Q1 product launches have a hard date (Feb 15). We need a firm commitment that the initial 48-GPU step (if we choose it) can be available by Jan 25 for load testing. Can Redwood commit to that activation gate?
3) SLA/credits: your note about warm-start exceptions — can you quantify the credit if you miss the activation date?

Also: could you send a version of the proposal with two rows for the minimum (32 vs 64) so finance can compare.

Morgan
VP Product, OrionBio
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@orionbio.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-14T13:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Provisioning scenarios & activation schedule — OrionBio dedicated capacity

Morgan —

Quick technical/ops note from the infra side so you can evaluate effort and risk:

- Jan 25 activation to reach initial 48 GPUs: feasible with standard lead-time if we schedule now. We'll provision a dedicated pool in our us-west-2 region and pre-warm a model staging slot. There is a 72–96 hour model warm-up window for KV cache fill if you need peak latency parity with long-running traffic.
- Minimum 32-GPU floor: we can model a blended rate sheet. Practically we can set reserved capacity at 32 GPUs and allow auto-burst to your contracted cap (64/96/128) with a defined unit price for burst tokens. That preserves predictability for finance while giving you headroom.
- Activation SLAs: we can commit to Jan 25 for the 48-GPU step if we receive signed docs by Jan 4 and an MLOps contact for model seeding. If we miss the activation window, standard practice is pro-rated credits on the reserved capacity for days missed; per your ask we can add a firm credit: 1% of monthly reserved fee per day missed beyond a 3-day cure window, up to 10% (this is a negotiable clause).

I've attached a quick activation_timeline.xlsx with the node ordering and ETA by week if you want to share with procurement.

Ben
Head of Capacity Ops — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Following Ben's notes, we've sketched a revised two-line commercial to present to your finance team:

- Plan 1 (Conservative): 32-GPU guaranteed / burst to 64 GPUs. Month-to-month activation pricing, 12-month term. Unit price higher, but minimal commitment.
- Plan 2 (Preferred): 64-GPU guaranteed / committed ramp to 96 over 10 weeks. Lower unit price; includes one week of pre-warm + two smoke test windows.

We will accept a Jan 25 soft-activation ETA for the 48-GPU test lane provided: signed order by Jan 4, MLOps contact details, and initial model checkpoint uploaded to our staging registry. I'll prepare a short addendum that codifies the activation credit Ben proposed (1% per missed day after 3-day cure, cap 10%).

Next steps from our side:
- I'll update the proposal with the two-line commercial and attach a DocuSign link.
- Laura will run the final pricing math and include a proposal-level summary for your CFO.

Can procurement aim to review the updated doc by Dec 22 so we can finalize before the holidays?
